items.title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
items.summary: Barclays is eliminating roughly 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, as it accelerates its adoption of artificial intelligence and concludes a three-year cost-cutting drive. Around 60% of the cuts will affect support functions, while the bank expects efficiency measures to yield £1.1bn in savings in 2027.

also.title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as bank steps up AI adoption
also.note: The Financial Times characterizes the cuts as Barclays stepping up AI adoption rather than attributing the layoffs to increasing reliance on it.

also.author: Samuel Norman
also.title: Barclays to axe 5,000 jobs by end of year after banking on AI savings
also.note: City AM highlights the year-end timeline and frames the bank as actively banking on AI savings to justify axing the positions.

brief.what: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 roles, equal to roughly 5% of its global workforce, having already closed 1,000 posts with 4,000 more reductions due by year-end. Around 60% of the cuts will target support functions, including developers.
brief.who: The actions are led by Barclays and Chief Executive CS Venkatakrishnan, with analyst commentary from Russ Mould at AJ Bell and Will Howlett at Quilter Cheviot.
brief.context: The reductions coincide with the conclusion of a three-year cost-cutting programme primarily focused on Barclays' UK retail bank, alongside its investment banking arm. The bank also posted a £2.3bn quarterly profit, which beat the prior year but missed forecasts.
brief.why: Barclays said the cuts stem from an ongoing modernisation plan and heavy investments in technology to simplify operations, calling AI the 'icing on the cake' of its strategy. Analysts noted banks' long-term technology investments are increasingly reducing the headcount needed to run operations.
brief.next: The bank expects its remaining 4,000 planned reductions to finish by the end of this year and anticipates its efficiency measures will deliver an additional £1.1bn of savings in 2027.
